verdict.rationale: Alma's homepage pairs its 98%+ approval figure with a stated basis, "across hundreds of cases", plus a disclaimer, and the founders page ties it to "hundreds of prior filings". That basis is a vague case count with no exact numbers, time window or methodology. A separate learn page advertises a different "99%+ approval rate" with no basis at all. Missing for 10: exact case counts, a stated time window, a described methodology (e.g., how RFEs, denials or withdrawals are counted), a consistent basis for the 99%+ figure on the learn page, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, any advertised approval or success rate comes with a stated basis — case counts, time window, or methodology — on the provider's own pages

citations.quote: Approval rates across hundreds of cases. Past success doesn’t guarantee future outcomes.
the firm's 98%+ approval rate is reinforced by case intelligence pulled from hundreds of prior filings
